This is exactly what I hoped for. When I pasted the same link again, instead of quietly making a second copy, it told me I'd already saved that address and brought up my existing bookmark — with my old notes still on it — ready to adjust. I changed the title, saved, and I still had just the one entry, now updated. No duplicate. That's the behavior I wanted.

Using the exact web address to recognize a repeat feels like a sensible starting point, and opening the existing one right there in the save flow is good.

One small thing I'll mention so it doesn't surprise us later — I don't need it solved now: the same page can sometimes hide behind slightly different addresses, like one with a trailing slash or a bunch of tracking gibberish tacked on the end. I noticed you already shrug off a trailing slash, which is nice. I'm fine treating exact-match as the rule for now; just wanted to flag it.

This one's good. What's next?
